content:
The image shows a soybean field with widespread yellowing/chlorosis on leaves. Key observations:

- Upper canopy leaves show green-to-yellow mottling and blotchiness
- The discoloration appears patchy and irregular across many plants
- Leaves show a mosaic-like pattern with yellow blotches against green background
- No discrete lesions with margins, no fungal growth, no necrotic spots
- Younger/upper leaves appear most affected with this mottled yellowing pattern
- Plants appear somewhat stunted compared to a healthy canopy

This mottled green-yellow pattern predominantly in the upper canopy, affecting younger leaves with a blotchy/mosaic appearance matches **Bean Pod Mottle Virus** very well. The symptom description notes "Green to yellow mottling (blotchiness) of younger leaves in the upper canopy" which is precisely what's visible here. The pattern doesn't fit the interveinal pattern of SDS (which would keep veins green while tissue between turns yellow), and it doesn't show the vein-associated symptoms of Soybean Vein Necrosis Virus.
